output.title: Spot duplicate emails before they become cleanup work
output.body:
This is for a CEO of a 1–10 person business who has tried ChatGPT but has not wired AI into a real workflow yet. The question is not “can AI fix duplicate emails?” It is: do the duplicates reach you before you act on them?

That is the bounded workflow decision. If duplicates only create a bit of cleanup later, you may not need anything more than a clear process. If they cause inconsistent replies, extra review time, or manual reconciliation, the problem is worth defining properly before you touch a tool.

Start with three recent examples. For each one, note where the duplicate came from: two systems syncing the same contact, the same person sending again, or you copying a thread into another tool. Then decide which duplicates must be caught before action and which can be cleaned up later. An invoice or payment request belongs in the first group; a newsletter usually does not. Human approval stays in place for anything involving money or other high-risk decisions.

One practical next step: run a one-week manual test. Put suspicious duplicates in one folder and review them by hand. Count the true repeats, the false positives, and the time your own review takes. If the pattern is messy, that is useful too. It usually means the next step is a clearer definition of “duplicate,” not a bigger tool.
